# Koshin Studio (English)

> A one-person studio by Koshin, a web and app engineer in Japan. I build free browser games and an iPhone app, and write development logs that report the numbers I measured, cite official sources with the date checked, and say plainly what I could not confirm. Every English article is a hand-checked translation of a Japanese original, linked from the article.

Site (English): https://koshinstudio.com/en/
Full text of the English pages: https://koshinstudio.com/en/llms-full.txt
Japanese index: https://koshinstudio.com/llms.txt

## Works (free browser games and apps)
- [Negaeri Shogi — a free 6×6 board game where sandwiched pieces defect](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/negaeri-shogi/): Negaeri Shogi is a free browser board game on a 6×6 board. Drop a piece to sandwich your opponent’s pieces: they defect to your side and get promoted, and chains flip many at once. Play locally, vs AI, or online with ratings.
- [Anime Type Quiz — find your anime type and the one anime that fits you](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/shindananime/): A free anime quiz. Answer 12 questions (up to 50), get your anime type from 6 axes (like RDCP-VM) and a nickname, and see your destined anime plus two runners-up chosen from over 6,000 real titles.
- [Toreca Dash (トレカダッシュ) — Japan TCG lottery, pre-order & restock alerts](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/torecadash/): An iPhone app that gathers lottery, pre-order and first-come sales of trading cards from stores across Japan, with a deadline calendar and alerts. Store information is mostly in Japanese.
- [Sushi Stack](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/sushitsumu/): Sushi Stack is a free browser merge puzzle. Drop rice, merge matching toppings up 11 tiers to reach the golden sushi tub. Online ranking, 14 languages, no install or sign-up.
- [Stop at exactly 10 seconds!](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/stopwatch10/): A free browser game: press start and count ten seconds in your head, with no numbers or sound on screen. Three modes, millisecond precision, and a fair daily ranking.
- [Draft Party — a free multiplayer draft game you play in your browser](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/draft-party/): Draft Party is a free browser game. Scout fictional rookies by their abilities and draw lots on ties, then watch several seasons of stats, standings and head-to-head results together. Play with friends or strangers, in four languages.
- [Kaeru Sekai (Returning World) — a free 3D game: bring a gray world back to green](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/kaeru-sekai/): A free 3D browser game. Plant seeds of light to bring a withered gray world back to green, then settle people and watch 100 years pass. Valleys, islands, deserts and volcanoes, generated from a number. No install.
- [Danmaku Maker — build and share bullet-hell stages (iPhone game)](https://koshinstudio.com/en/works/danmaku-maker/): A free iPhone and iPad bullet-hell game in 10 languages: build stages with up to 8 emitters, publish them, and play stages made by players worldwide. Four modes, 30 official stages.

## Tools (calculators)
- [Gacha completion calculator](https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha/): How many pulls, and how much money, to collect every type. The average, the pulls by which 90% of people finish, and whether a complete set is cheaper.
- [Gacha drop rate and pity calculator](https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/gacha-rate/): From the drop rate, how many pulls until you get it. Supports how many copies you want and a pity (guaranteed after N pulls).
- [TCG booster box price per pack calculator](https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/box-price/): Turn a booster box or set price into a price per pack and compare it with the list price. Typical pack counts per box for each game, counted from 179 listings.
- [Lottery win chance calculator](https://koshinstudio.com/en/calc/lottery/): From the odds and the number of entries, the chance you win at least once. Works even when each entry has different odds.

## Notes (development logs; each has a Markdown version at the article URL + index.md)
- [How bullet-hell patterns work: ring, aimed, rain, spiral and homing, with formulas and live demos](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/danmaku-patterns/): The exact math behind ring, aimed (odd vs even), rain, spiral and homing bullet-hell patterns, from a real danmaku game, with live demos.
- [Sushi Stack scores stopped reaching the leaderboard: I changed the game’s numbers and forgot the server’s re-check (twice)](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/rank-verify-mismatch/): Honest runs of a browser game stopped reaching the online leaderboard: two game values changed without updating the server that re-checks scores. The fix, and a test that compares both sides with the same seeds.
- [Japanese Pokémon card & TCG lottery apps compared: Toreca Dash, Toreget, NowPokeca, Pokeka Tracker and Toreca no Chizu](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/tcg-lottery-app-compare/): Five apps and sites that track Pokémon card and TCG lotteries, pre-orders and restocks at stores in Japan, compared on games, alerts, maps and price — by the developer of one of them, weak points included.
- [An aggregator crawl read only page 1: card articles were on pages 2–4, and only the first 6,000 characters went to the AI](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/aggregator-pagination/): The crawl of a stock-information aggregator read only page 1 (mostly consoles), while Pokémon and Gundam articles were on later pages. Only the first 6,000 characters went to the AI, so later stores dropped. I followed 12 pages and read all the text.
- [“Not just noticing; not letting it happen”: turning a report-only monitor into one that fills gaps on the spot](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/fill-the-gap/): The gap monitor only reported and nothing was filled until a person noticed. I made it create missing articles on the spot, logged a branch that dropped silently, and showed how to apply even with no link. Coverage went from 92% to 100%.
- [The same report for the third time: a SwiftUI button responded only on its text, and my two earlier “fixes” did nothing](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/swiftui-hit-area/): The “Won” and “Lost” buttons responded only on the text. Two earlier fixes (modifier order) did not work; I built the look inside a ButtonStyle and replaced six places. A mail-order article with coordinates had the same kind of root.
- [“Weird articles keep multiplying”: I counted by creation route and closed the entrances, and my counting was wrong twice](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/weird-articles-by-route/): 252 displayed lotteries were counted by route. Ended rounds left in an aggregator’s table were imported daily with empty deadlines (33); links to search results or top pages and deadlines disagreeing with the store’s own row were closed at the entrance.
- [“Automate everything that can be”: counting showed 66 repair jobs had never run on a schedule, and I added only six](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/automate-sorted/): Matching 319 HTTP endpoints against 184 scheduled jobs by call showed 66 that only ran by hand. After a dry run I scheduled only the continuously needed ones, six, and fixed a queue that let the same job pile up.
- [“The server went down and I cannot recover it” was wrong: only inbound SSH had been blocked](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/misdiagnosis-down/): From 3:10 a.m. I could not connect to the server and judged it stopped. In fact its processes had run for over 7 days, all 192 scheduled jobs were normal, and only inbound SSH was blocked.
- [“ヤマダ電機” versus “ヤマダデンキ”: spelling variants and duplicates had three overlapping causes](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/store-name-variants/): Store names compared only by “contains”, deadlines differing by 59 seconds, and a manual-only dedupe job. I used a general comparison key instead of a synonym table, ran it hourly, and found two dangers in testing.
- [“One page = one case” was false: articles of a shop taking 6 products on one form were hidden just for sharing a link](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/one-page-many-cases/): A job that decided duplicates by link alone hid 5 of 6 articles of a shop taking 6 products on one Google Form. I changed it to link + product. I also found the server’s “entry tiers” were never read by the app.
- [English and katakana names share no characters: a fingerprint gate rejected 42 correct matches](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/transliteration-gate/): The market-price link rate fell to 39%. The products existed on the market site, but my English names and its katakana names share no characters, so 42 matches were rejected in 26 hours. I kept the gate and added a narrow second judgement for this match only.
- [Looking up an ambiguous store name returns Shizuoka, the middle of Japan: I judged by Google’s own answer, not a list of chains](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/geocode-shizuoka/): Passing a store name to Google’s place search with a rectangle covering Japan returned its middle (Shizuoka/Aichi) for ambiguous names. Instead of a list of chain names I judged trust from the answer itself with four rules.
- [If you throw failure away, the screen lies: a calendar that said “registered” with none added, a frozen OCR, a notification without a store name](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/swallowed-failure/): try? discarded failures, so the calendar showed “registered N events” with 0 added and could never register again, OCR failure froze the screen, and the notification buffer forgot the store name.
- [Candidates were found, yet reading the answer failed every time: a URL cut at 200 tokens, and a search that returned 400 on hyphens](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/truncated-answer/): An AI reply choosing an official announcement page was cut at 200 tokens and failed every time. The result stayed 0 because store announcements name no product and the AI obeyed my instruction. Rakuten’s search returned 400 depending on hyphen position.
- [A function named “load from iCloud if newer” compared nothing: a 20-record history could become 1](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/icloud-overwrite/): The iCloud sync function never checked whether data was newer and replaced everything. A fresh device with an empty state could overwrite another device’s 20 records with 1. I added update-time comparison and never overwrite with empty.
- [With no ads, 25 real-device checks were blocked: test ads in developer mode only, and no hard-coded prize names](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/test-ads/): Before ads were served, 25 of 163 real-device checklist items could not be verified. In developer mode only, the app switches to Google’s test ad units. Prize names are read from one setting and never hard-coded, including in the checklist.
- [“That’s just a Beyblade” came back after I added a gate: the blocked value leaked in another form](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/leaked-value/): A gate “do not create a product whose name contains a toy’s name” was bypassed because the AI’s product name lost the toy’s name. I moved the judgement to the announcement body and rejected only when no card-game word appears.
- [Checks that logged “deferred to next run” had never run: three time budgets counted from the same start](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/budget-starved/): A process had three stages whose time budgets were counted from the same start time, so the rotating 25 checks ran 0 times each run. “Deferred 18 items” meant all of them. I allocated from the job’s time limit and logged each step’s time.
- [I fixed a timeout three times and it did not stop: the culprit was a second process under the same lock](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/timeout-third-fix/): A Rakuten Books stock check timed out 17 times a day. Limiting fetches, then a whole item, did not help; the third time I found that another process under the same lock re-fetched everything with no time limit.
- [“It gets cleaned up later” hid an entrance bug: 400 near-identical products were re-created every day](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/cleanup-hides-entrance/): Catalogue registration looked up existing products by exact name only, so brackets, spaces and full/half-width differences re-created near-identical products daily: 437 in one day, 410 with no articles. The nightly merge job hid it.
- [A secret token was in the logs in plain text: scrub at the one exit that cannot be forgotten](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/secret-in-logs/): An HTTP library put the request URL in its error message, so a scraping-service token reached the logs. My earlier scrubbing function worked only where called, and there are over 50 callers. I moved the scrubbing to the single exit every log passes through.
- [Moving from Cloud Functions to a ¥4,300 server: ¥3,700 a day, Yahoo! failing in the EEA, and five traps](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/vps-migration/): After the free trial, Cloud Functions cost about ¥3,700 a day because waiting time was billed. I moved almost unchanged code to a Singapore VPS (about ¥4,300 a month). Helsinki failed because Yahoo! blocks the EEA; there were 15 secrets, not 5.
- [I opened the links of displayed articles and compared them: about 60 mistakes, and three mistakes in my own first check](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/destination-check/): Opening more than 1,000 destination pages and comparing with the articles: Amazon invitation requests shown as first-come, closed or sold-out items displayed, links to other stores or products, application links redirecting to a site’s top page. My first check was wrong in three ways too.
- [Four things from a full sweep of 61 audits: 51 jobs clumped at 4 a.m., a lock that expired in 55 seconds, and a price-filling idea I decided not to add](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/audit-sweep-61/): Once-a-day jobs clumped at 27 at 4 o’clock and 24 at 5; a Rakuten patrol took 181–480 s per run with a 55-second lock; I stopped counting anomalies that cannot be fixed; and I measured a way to fill official prices from one store but did not add it.
- [Comparing with other sites to count gaps: the first “23% coverage” was a measuring mistake and the truth was 49%](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/coverage-check/): Counting whether I show lotteries other sites list: the first 23% was distorted by product-name spelling and expired articles. After fixing it, 49%; after fixing five gap-filling problems, 90%. Sites whose terms prohibit automated fetching were not imported.
- [Four gaps in monitoring X: posts missing from search, accounts that change hands, a store-finding query, and catching up after an outage](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/x-monitoring-gaps/): Four stores’ lottery posts did not appear in search even after 751 posts; a registered store had become a person; store-finding found 11 of 63; and after a 6-day outage only 185 of 2,866 were read in 2 hours. Fixes and cost estimates.
- [When you cannot watch everything quickly: popular 128 of 427 sets run fast, and the fastest lane yields to the budget](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/hot-lane/): Full laps over 427 sets took 4 to 24 hours. A separate lane for 128 popular sets and truly once-a-minute checks for popular items; batching stopped another monitor and measuring over a short window misjudged cost.
- [Fixing a gate does not fix existing data: a “tried already” mark, a URL marker and a lookup table](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/fix-the-existing-data/): After fixing a judgement, 12 of 32 existing articles stayed wrong (the skip mark lasts 7 days); a marker stored in the URL was lost on link rewrite and 111 articles were split again; removing a table key left written values. Five reports had one shape.
- [Fixing product genre from the official catalogue: three dry runs took 13 changes down to 4](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/genre-from-catalog/): A Duel Masters product was registered as Pokémon. Making the official catalogue the source of truth, my first dry run would have moved nine correct Weiss Schwarz products to another game; after three dry runs there were 0 misfires.
- [393 “work-name-only” products from an official list: the name field did not contain the product form](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/catalog-seed-393/): An official-list import created 502 products in one day (usually 1–10). The name field held only the work name; the form was in the category. Cleaning 393 and re-registering 328 correct names took alias collisions from 0 pairs to 250.
- [Online play that trusts nothing the client says: the server decides moves, clocks and results](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/negaeri-online/): Online play without login. Moves are validated by the rules engine, the clock lives only on the server, a disconnect gets 30 seconds, tokens are signed with HMAC, and ratings use pre-match numbers. With real values from the server code.
- [“The same application page” does not mean “the same store”: 52 articles showed another store’s name](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/same-page-not-same-store/): A job that unified store names across articles sharing an application page turned a Sendai store into “Shinjuku South Exit”. One page was shared by 15 separate stores. I changed it to unify only when confirmed the same place and restored 52 articles from an untouched field.
- [When first-come sales start, the site becomes a waiting-room page: a 15 KB notice slipped through an 8,000-byte gate](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/waiting-room/): On AEON Style Online, a first-come sale turned the whole site into a 15 KB “heavy access” page. It passed the 8,000-byte check added earlier that day and was read as “success, 0 products”. I switched to a title check; Amazon’s 13 minutes were serial AI screening.
- [Before widening concurrency slots: widening a 2-core server from 8 to 14, and the earlier conclusion that was half wrong](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/concurrency-slots/): Shortening intervals made the 1-minute first-come monitor wait for a slot. I widened slots from 8 to 11 and 14 and measured. The real cap was not CPU but jobs sleeping on Rakuten API’s 1.5-second wait while holding slots.
- [Three mix-ups in splitting one article into products: a child treated as a parent, a shared link pointing to another store, a name owned by two products](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/split-mixups/): Reprocessing a split “child” hid 60 lotteries closing that day (23 stores); a link-only lookup shared by 13 stores picked another store’s parent; names claimed by two products numbered 267 pairs. Real items vanished with nothing on screen.
- [Four times my own tools hurt me: a summary dropped conditions, one undefined stopped saving, a check locked out production, alerts that never cleared](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/self-inflicted/): A “15 characters” prompt dropped entry conditions in 671 checked lotteries; one undefined broke every save and burned 41% of a day’s credits; six parallel requests got the production IP blocked; I made alerts that kept ringing after the fix.
- [Every deploy re-ran the daily jobs: 477 runs in 48 hours, 46.6% of that day’s Gemini cost](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/rerun-on-deploy/): A once-a-day job ran 43 times and used 46.6% of a day’s Gemini cost. Timed-out runs never wrote their last-run time, so every restart treated them as missed. A deploy at 08:00 also swallowed the digest.
- [Notifications cannot be recalled: 19% of the last 72 hours’ notifications were wrong, and the gate worked after the fact](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/notify-gate/): Of 644 notifications in 72 hours, 122 (19%) were wrong. The article gate hides articles later, but a notification goes out about 0.6 seconds after saving; 25 of 30 hidden articles had already been pushed. I put the same gate at the notification entrance.
- [A “1-minute” monitor checked each item once per 10 minutes: before speeding up, count the revisit interval and what was delivered](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/interval-vs-delivery/): A first-come monitor watched 63 items but checked 4–9 per run, so each item once per 10 minutes, and caught 3 sales in 7 days. Shortening other intervals slowed it further, and “not screened” meant 45% of first-come listings got no notification.
- [Four real lotteries silently thrown away: a regex, dates without a year, batched answers and null](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/silent-discard/): “x.com” matched “e-starbox.com” so application links were never used; a date with no year was read as 2020 so no Pokémon items were imported; batched answers got out of step; “cannot decide” was read as “none” and nearly hid 129 lotteries.
- [“Checked” marks on articles that had never been read: the t.co relay page](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/tco-relay/): Opened with a browser User-Agent, t.co returned a relay page instead of redirecting. All 220 displayed articles were unread and 9 were closed forms. How I fixed it and how I removed the wrong “checked” marks.
- [Before cutting Gemini cost, I doubted the meter: price, breakdown and cache were all wrong, and the cache threshold changed when I re-measured](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/gemini-meter/): The cost meter was broken in three places (prices under-reported 2.6×, 31 purposes merged, cache uncounted). The cache threshold was about 8,000 tokens in September and about 4,000 in October. Padding the prompt shifted 9% of answers.
- [Firestore cost in yen: 91% of reads came from one place, and my first cache did not work](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/firestore-91/): Seen in yen for the first time, Firestore cost about ¥13,000 a month, close to Gemini. 91% of reads were a product list re-read for every post. A 60-second cache failed because 32 jobs ran at once; caching the pending promise fixed it.
- [Setting the rules of Negaeri Shogi by playing AI against AI: one change that worked, six that broke](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/negaeri-balance/): A 6×6 board game where sandwiched pieces defect. Instead of guessing the numbers, I ran 40 to 100 AI-vs-AI games per rule. Flips per move went from 2% to 81%, removing the king guard ended games in 17 moves, and the first-move edge is still unsolved.
- [Pokémon card sleeves and loaders: sizes and what “pt” means](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/card-supplies-guide/): What to check before buying Pokémon card sleeves, toploaders and deck boxes: standard vs small size, what 35pt means, and a buying checklist. Not a hands-on review; unverified points are listed.
- [ITMS-91064 “Invalid Binary”: NSPrivacyTracking was true but NSPrivacyTrackingDomains was empty](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/itms-91064/): An iOS build was rejected by Apple's automated review with ITMS-91064. NSPrivacyTracking was true while NSPrivacyTrackingDomains was an empty array. How it was fixed, and what was not verified.
- [App Store review sent “Guideline 2.1 Information Needed”: the six things Apple asked for](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/review-info-needed/): My first App Store submission got a request for more information (Guideline 2.1), not a rejection. The six things Apple asked for and how they connect to earlier fixes.
- [Firebase 12 does not work with Xcode 15.2 (Swift 6.0 required): why I pinned Firebase 11.4.0 and AdMob 11.5.0](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/xcode152-sdk/): On an old Mac stuck on Xcode 15.2, newer Firebase and AdMob SDKs fail to build. Which versions break, which I pinned (Firebase 11.4.0, AdMob 11.5.0), and why.
- [iOS app freezes and is killed (0x8BADF00D): a SwiftUI computed property ran on every redraw](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/torecadash-watchdog/): An iOS app was force-quit by the watchdog (0x8BADF00D). A SwiftUI computed property re-filtered and re-sorted 951 articles on the main thread every body evaluation.
- [No builds arriving in TestFlight: I had used up the 25 free Xcode Cloud hours (my first diagnosis was wrong)](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/torecadash-ci/): New builds stopped appearing in TestFlight. My first diagnosis (“[ci skip] is blocking builds”) was wrong; the workflow built the iOS app on every commit.
- [Firebase Auth: force-quitting the app created anonymous accounts in bulk (waiting for currentUser to restore)](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/apple-signin/): Force-quitting the app made Firebase create a new anonymous account each launch: 17 of 19 users were throwaway. Cause: reading currentUser too early.
- [A canvas becomes twice as large on Retina: inset:0 does not stretch it (a bug in a logo that bursts when you tap it)](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/logo-pop/): Burst particles appeared in the wrong place on high-DPI screens. A canvas with only inset:0 keeps its pixel size, so it was 2x larger in CSS on Retina.
- [I counted “duplicates are practically zero,” but the audit reported 112 pairs](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/dup-zero/): A nightly merge job timed out partway through the first genre, so later genres were never reached. My count of zero saw only that genre. Fixed with a rotating budget.
- [Making a 10-second stopwatch ranking fair: 3 decimals, ties and write counts](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/stopwatch-rank/): Why I truncate to three decimals so coarse clocks get no advantage, how ties (a 1/333 chance) are broken, and how I counted KV writes on the free tier.
- [From 16,177 titles to 6,091: how the anime quiz database was built by dropping over 60%](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/anime-db/): An anime quiz picks from about 6,000 titles. Where they came from, the criterion that cut 62.3% of 16,177, what remains, and the biases of the method.
- [“80% was chosen over 82%”: the quiz’s match percentage disagreed with its ranking](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/match-percent/): An anime quiz’s match percentage used a different yardstick from its ranking. With the old display, 35 to 40% of 1,000 synthetic respondents saw a reversed top 3.
- [The streaming buttons were shown even for titles you could not watch: making the quiz result screen true](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/result-screen/): The anime quiz showed the same two streaming buttons for every title; about 29% were wrong. How I narrowed buttons by availability and fixed image problems.
- [Cutting six buttons to one: first-time players did not know what to press](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/first-visit/): A browser game title screen had six things to press. I made the first step one button, and fixed saves vanishing inside an iframe and play continuing in a hidden tab.
- [A typo born once multiplied across shops: the “30th SEREBRATION” incident](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/typo-catalog/): A misspelled product created once was reused as an existing product for every shop. Fixing 13 articles, exact-match prevention, and the limits of a safety net.
- [The “9-pack set” was nine different products: the same product that never matched](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/torecadash-9set/): Matching my app against roundup sites showed 54% of lotteries displayed: a product mix-up, an asymmetric name key and an article ID that blocked new rounds.
- [Splitting a “9-pack set” by contents created 80 fake products](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/fake-products/): One real product was split by its contents, creating 80 products that do not exist. Stopping the entry, restoring 22 parents, detaching 190 children and an audit.
- [Measuring Qiita’s “posting too frequently” limit: a new account could not create another article for about 30 minutes](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/qiita-post-interval/): After publishing, a new Qiita account could not create the next article. Checking the editor every 5 minutes, two measurements gave about 30 minutes; one was lost.
- [Rejected by CrazyGames with no reason given: I recorded the game and found four problems](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/crazygames/): A game portal rejected my game with only “overall quality below expectations.” I recorded what the reviewer saw, found four causes and fixed them by measuring.
- [Japanese text garbled in the CrazyGames preview: the file was correct, the cause was never found, so I escaped to ASCII](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/ascii-text/): One character broke in a game portal’s preview though the file bytes were correct. How I made the game immune without finding the cause.
- [Works on my machine, breaks when deployed: four incidents shipping a static site to Cloudflare Pages](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/deploy-gotchas/): Stale cache, breadcrumbs that multiplied each build, a symlink into my own environment, and local-only images: four deploy incidents on Cloudflare Pages.
- [Comparing static site hosts by their official terms: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages and Firebase Hosting](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/hosting-compare/): Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages and Firebase Hosting compared by official terms (Oct 2026): ads allowed, free limits, file limits, config.
- [Comparing comment systems for static sites by their official information: giscus, utterances, Disqus, Remark42 and more](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/comment-services/): giscus, utterances, Disqus, Remark42, Cusdis, Staticman and Commento compared by official pages (Oct 2026): storage, ads and tracking, maintenance status.
- [Comparing iOS ad SDKs and Firebase by their official information: AdMob, AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay and Supabase](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/ios-sdk-compare/): AdMob, AppLovin MAX, LevelPlay, Firebase and Supabase compared by official pages (Oct 2026): payouts, privacy manifests, minimum Xcode, free tiers.
- [Claude API vs Gemini API by official numbers: small-model prices, web search, spend limits and deprecation](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/claude-vs-gemini-api/): Claude and Gemini API compared by official pages (Oct 2026): small-model prices, web search cost and caps, spend limits, deprecation notice.
- [Migrating from the Claude API to the Gemini API (gemini-3.1-flash-lite): 16 call sites into one function](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/gemini-migration/): Moving an iOS app backend from Claude Haiku 4.5 to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite: choosing by deprecation date, one wrapper, a search cap breaker, a kill switch.
- [It let things through when it could not check: how “fail-open” brought in resale items](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/fail-open/): A gate that let items pass when the list price could not be confirmed had a blind spot: a daily search cap. Telling “did not know” from “could not look.”
- [What I read as “fetched” was just a notice page: three days of zero products](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/blocked-page/): A scraper returned zero products for three days because a 2,410-byte “enable JavaScript” page counted as success. How I centralized the check.
- [I could not listen, so I measured the waveform: building Japanese instruments with WebAudio for Sushi Stack](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/webaudio/): A browser game with no audio files: koto, taiko and gong synthesized with WebAudio. I could not listen, so I set volume by measuring waveform peaks.
- [Making a ranking server use only half of the free tier: from 5 calls to 2](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/ranking-free-tier/): A game ranking on Workers and D1: calls per play from 5 to 2, rows read from 421 to 221. Server-side rank counting and removing the preflight call.
- [Four things that stopped my iOS app before App Review: iPad screenshots, ITMS-91064, account deletion, reporting posts](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/torecadash-review/): Before submitting an iOS app, four things stopped me: iPad screenshots, ITMS-91064, account deletion (5.1.1(v)) and user-content reporting (1.2), and how I fixed each.
- [I re-measured a “nothing can be done” assumption and scraping cost dropped to one eighth](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/scrape-cost/): I believed two sites could not be fetched more often because of cost. Comparing three Scrape.do settings showed rendering was wasted: 3x faster, 1/8 the credits.
- [A bulk update hit “all articles”: count before you write, and break your tests to prove they work](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/bulk-accident/): A bulk job hit every article and wrongly restored 18 items. How I reverted them from status history and proved new tests work by breaking rules one at a time.
- [Python splitlines() breaks JSONL: the culprit was U+2028, an invisible line separator](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/u2028/): Python splitlines() broke a JSONL file because 2 of 7,247 records contained U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR). Why it happens and the one-line fix: split on the newline only.
- [“It should shrink” was wrong twice: cutting AI calls and what I measured afterward](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/torecadash-ai/): Reducing calls to an AI in a trading-card app: a predicted 45% cut was 4.5%, and batching ran zero times after deploy. What I found by recounting, with numbers.
- [What changes when an anime quiz goes from 50 questions to 12?](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/shindan12/): A 50-question anime quiz now gives a result after 12. Measured with 1,000 synthetic respondents: the type mostly matches, but the single recommended title changes a lot.
- [“The pile settles at 89%” was wrong: my measurement was what was wrong](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/sushi-measure/): Rebalancing a merge puzzle, I found my measurement had counted falling pieces. Three causes: a backward size ladder, a pit-shaped tub, and pieces tunneling the floor.
- [Measuring the gap between ads in time, not in plays](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/adgap/): Why I replaced “one ad every 5 plays” with “7 minutes since the last ad” in a browser game, how it behaves, and what I still do not know.
- [The conger eel was too big: finding why a merge puzzle’s last piece was out of reach](https://koshinstudio.com/en/notes/anago/): I could never reach my puzzle’s last piece. Statistics from hundreds of auto-played games showed the real cause: everything was too big for the tub.
